# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for PAN-4534

# Review — PAN-4534
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — the new `trigger` fallback turns a cancelled (superseded) check run into "CI FAILED" feedback for the PR's new head, and that feedback then debounces the head's real failure

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-4534-review-f4d0db0b
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4534/.pan/review/agent-pan-4534-review-f4d0db0b/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-4534 / /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4534
- PR: #4613
- HEAD reviewed: f4d0db0bd8888a0f8e1608cdf6580100d6303b72
- Base / prior cycle SHA: merge-base 010f8e710a64e38a97b67461f71a9cbb822f3706; no prior review cycle

## Blocking Findings

### [correctness] The `trigger` fallback reports cancelled / stale / startup-failure check runs as CI failures — `src/lib/webhook-handlers.ts:285` and `src/lib/cloister/ci-failure-feedback.ts:704`
- Severity: ! (MUST)
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect; in_pr_scope (introduced by this PR's `trigger` fallback). It also over-applies FR-1, which says the fallback reports "the failed check that the `check_run` webhook fired on"; a cancelled check is not a failed check.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: `handleCheckRun` calls the relay for every conclusion in `FAILING_CHECK_CONCLUSIONS` (`webhook-handlers.ts:136`: `FAILURE, ERROR, TIMED_OUT, CANCELLED, ACTION_REQUIRED, STARTUP_FAILURE, STALE`). That was already true on main. The PR now attaches `trigger` for each of these conclusions without checking which one it is (`webhook-handlers.ts:285-291`). In the relay, `collectCheckRunFailures` keeps only `conclusion === 'failure'`, and `listFailingRuns` keeps only `--status failure`. So for a cancelled job both lookups return nothing. The new block at `ci-failure-feedback.ts:704-707` then adds the cancelled trigger as a failure. The guard that skips feedback when nothing failed (`failures.length === 0 && … && opts.source !== 'polling_reconciliation'`) no longer applies, so feedback is written and the agent is messaged.
- Expected / observed / impact: Before this PR, a check_run with no failing check run and no failed workflow run logged "No failing runs found … skipping feedback" and sent nothing. Now the work agent receives `SPECIALIST FEEDBACK: ci-monitor reported CI FAILED … fix ALL failing checks`, with a feedback file that lists the cancelled check under "Failing checks (1)" and "*(No log excerpt available.)*". This happens on ordinary pushes in this repo: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:16-18` sets `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true`. So when an agent pushes while CI is still running on its previous commit, the old commit's in-progress jobs conclude `cancelled`. GitHub attaches each of those cancelled check runs to the PR **with the PR's current head sha** (live evidence below). So `handleCheckRun` calls the relay with `headSha` set to the *new* head, whose CI is still pending. Both lookups for the new head come back empty, and the cancelled trigger is delivered as a failure **of the new head**. `lastNotifiedSha` is then set to the new head. This causes two harms: (1) a false "CI FAILED" directive about a commit whose CI has not finished, and (2) when the new head later really fails, the same-head debounce (`ci-failure-feedback.ts:680-686`) skips the real feedback, unless that failure is a newly counted CI test-gate failure. So lint/build failures in this repo, and every failure in a project that does not run its tests on CI, are suppressed.
- Evidence: (a) I ran an isolated probe in the scratchpad (a copy of `tests/unit/lib/cloister/ci-failure-feedback.test.ts` with one extra case, not committed). The setup was one check run `{ name: 'test-shard (4/4)', conclusion: 'cancelled' }`, `gh run list` → `[]`, and a relay called with `trigger: { name: 'test-shard (4/4)', url, jobId: 456 }` and source `check_run:test-shard (4/4)`. Result: `written=true messaged=1`, and the body contains `## Failing checks (1)` / `### test-shard (4/4)` / `Fix the failing checks…`. On main the same inputs reach the skip branch because `trigger` does not exist there (static trace of the diff: the push at lines 704-707 is the only new path). (b) A live read-only check on this PR: CI run 40113301716 on the superseded commit f4ff7fbc was cancelled when f4d0db0b was pushed. Its cancelled check run `test-shard (1/4)` (id 120929365327) reads `{"conclusion":"cancelled","head_sha":"f4ff7fbc…","pull_requests":[{"number":4613,"head":"f4d0db0bd888…"}]}`. The webhook therefore hands the relay PR #4613 at head f4d0db0b, whose own CI run (40113548904) is still pending. `isAdvisoryCheckName` matches only `coderabbit`, so these checks are not filtered out. Limitation: I did not deliver a live webhook end to end. The chain is the unit probe plus the live payload shape plus a static trace of `handleCheckRun`.
- Fix: Attach `trigger` (or use it in the relay) only for conclusions that are real failures. Pass the trigger's conclusion through and use it only for `failure` / `timed_out` (and `error` if you want). Do not use it for `cancelled`, `stale`, `action_required` or `startup_failure`; those keep today's skip. Add a test: a `cancelled` check_run with both lookups empty writes no feedback and sends no message. Optionally, make `collectCheckRunFailures` also treat `timed_out` as a failure (see the non-blocking note below).

## Non-blocking Findings

- `~` **Inherited-from-main tagging uses only main's tip commit** (`ci-failure-feedback.ts:697-700`, `listFailingCheckRunNames(owner, repo, 'main')`). `commits/main/check-runs` reads only the check runs of main's newest commit. When I checked, main's tip carried only a `Mintlify Deployment` check run, because its CI had not reported yet. So a shard failing on main is tagged `[INHERITED FROM MAIN]` only when main's newest commit has finished CI with that failure. Workflow-run names (`CI`) still never match job names. This is better than before but not reliable. Critique round 2 suggested `readDefaultBranchFailingTestChecks` (`ci-default-branch-tests.ts`), which already resolves failing test check names on the default branch, so it may be the sturdier source.
- `~` **`timed_out` jobs are not found by the check-run path** (`ci-check-run-failures.ts`, `conclusion === 'failure'`). A shard that hits `timeout-minutes` concludes `timed_out`. The check-run lookup skips it, and the workflow-run fallback finds it only after the whole run completes. Once the blocker fix exists, the trigger would at least name it. Consider including `timed_out` in the failing set.
- `~` **Log reads are serial and retry every error** (`ci-check-run-failures.ts:104-116, 132-143`). Each failing job can wait about 120 s. Jobs are read one after another inside `withIssueQueue`, so N unpublished logs delay this issue's later relays (including `recordCiTestGatePass`) by about N × 2 min. Rate-limit (403/429) and `maxBuffer` errors are retried as if they were a 404. This is documented as per-job in FR-4 and the docs, so it is not a spec violation. Reading the logs concurrently, or stopping the retry on non-404 errors, would bound the delay.
- `~` **Same-head debounce hides a later failed shard** (`ci-failure-feedback.ts:680-686`). Pre-existing, filed as [PAN-4625](https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/issues/4625), and excluded by non-goal 1. CodeRabbit marked it Major. I agree it is real, but it is outside this PR's scope.
- `?` **Advisory checks are not filtered on the check-run path.** `handleCheckRun` skips relays for advisory checks (`isAdvisoryCheckName`). But `collectCheckRunFailures` lists every failing check run, including advisory ones and non-Actions apps, and asks the agent to fix them. The old `gh run list` path had a similar problem (whole-workflow logs), so the impact is about equal. Filtering with `isAdvisoryCheckName` would be consistent.
- `?` **Memory per relay**: each failing job's log (`maxBuffer` 16 MiB) stays in memory until `withoutAggregateChecks` runs. With 4 failing shards that is up to about 64 MiB at once. This is bounded and short-lived, so it is advisory.
- `?` The first line of an Actions log starts with a UTF-8 BOM (confirmed on a live job log), so the timestamp-strip regex misses that one line. It is harmless because that line is runner setup.
- CodeRabbit comments at `ci-check-run-failures.ts:108` (projection) and `ci-failure-feedback.ts:514` (inherited names) were raised on 721cc998 and are addressed at HEAD (the `CHECK_RUN_FIELDS` projection, and `listFailingCheckRunNames`; see the partial-coverage note above). The `webhook-handlers.ts:291` comment matches the blocker above.

## Coverage

Changed-file ledger:
| File | Status |
| --- | --- |
| src/lib/cloister/ci-check-run-failures.ts | reviewed — projection, pagination, aggregate filter, excerpt extraction, retry loop |
| src/lib/cloister/ci-failure-feedback.ts | reviewed — collectFailures ordering, mainFailingNames, trigger fallback, body lines, debounce and skip interaction |
| src/lib/webhook-handlers.ts | reviewed — trigger construction; traced FAILING_CHECK_CONCLUSIONS and the detached dispatch in routes/webhooks.ts |
| src/lib/cloister/__tests__/ci-check-run-failures.test.ts | reviewed — included by the vitest `src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts` glob |
| tests/unit/lib/cloister/ci-failure-feedback.test.ts | reviewed — fake timers used for retries (repo rule met); no cancelled/non-failure trigger case |
| tests/unit/lib/webhook-handlers.test.ts | reviewed |
| docs/PIPELINE-GATES.md | reviewed — accurate except it does not say the trigger fallback should apply only to failed checks |
| .pan/drafts/pan-4534.md, -critique.md, -critique-2.md | reviewed — PRD, critique responses |
| .pan/specs/…PAN-4534….xbrief.json, .pan/continues/PAN-4534.xbrief.json | not applicable — planning artifacts; traces match the PRD |

Dimensions:
- Correctness: one blocker (cancelled trigger). The aggregate filter matches the real `test`/`lint` aggregate echo format in `ci.yml:144, 285-286` (raw log lines `<ts> test-shard: failure`). I checked live that `gh api …/actions/jobs/<id>/logs` follows the redirect and prints the log, and that the `--paginate --jq` projection prints one object per line.
- Security: no new trust boundary. `gh` is called through `execFile` with argv (no shell). Owner/repo come from the tracked webhook repository, and the job id is numeric from the GitHub API. The regex built from a check name escapes metacharacters. No findings.
- Performance: dispatch is detached after the 200 response (`routes/webhooks.ts`), so the event loop is not blocked. There is per-issue queue latency from serial retries (advisory), and bounded memory (advisory).
- Requirements/UX: see the AC matrix.

AC-to-evidence matrix:
| AC | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. In-progress run: feedback names the failing test file and title | met | test "names the failing test file and title…"; focused run passed |
| 2. Aggregate + shard: reports the shard, not the echo | met | test "reports the shard's failure, not the aggregate…" + unit tests for `withoutAggregateChecks` |
| 3. 404 then available: excerpt included (fake timers) | met | test "retries a job log that is not published yet…" |
| 4. No log ever: lists failing check names and URLs | met | test "lists the failing check names and URLs when no job log ever appears" |
| 5. PIPELINE-GATES.md describes the feedback | met | docs bullet "What the CI failure feedback contains (PAN-4534)" |
| FR-1 trigger fallback = "the failed check" | unmet for non-failure conclusions | blocker above (probe) |
| Non-goal 1: no change to when the relay fires | met (firing unchanged) | the same events call the relay, but delivery changed: cancelled events that used to skip now deliver (blocker above) |

## Verification
- `npx vitest run src/lib/cloister/__tests__/ci-check-run-failures.test.ts tests/unit/lib/cloister/ci-failure-feedback.test.ts tests/unit/lib/webhook-handlers.test.ts` → 3 files, 94 tests passed.
- Isolated probe (scratchpad copy of the relay test plus a cancelled-trigger case) → feedback written and agent messaged (blocker evidence).
- `npm run lint:effect-diagnostics` → passed (229 known findings; none new).
- `npm run typecheck` → root `tsc`, hooks, evals and dashboard-types all passed. `typecheck:frontend` failed with 1827 "Cannot find module" errors (`@tanstack/react-query`, `sonner`, `@testing-library/react`). That is a frontend dependency-resolution problem in this workspace, and the PR touches no frontend file. The acp/account/share stages did not run because the chain stopped. CI owns frontend strict tsc.
- CI on the PR head: `gh pr checks` shows only Mintlify (skipped) and CodeRabbit (pass). The `CI` workflow run 40113548904 for f4d0db0b is still `pending`, so the CI test job is **unverified**. I found no `overdeck/verification` check on this head.
- Live read-only `gh api` probes: the job-log endpoint redirect works; main's tip check runs carry only Mintlify.
- The full test suite was not run, per the review role.
